reason: The text explicitly establishes and emphasizes strict hierarchy throughout. God calls Moses and Aaron specifically to relay divine commands (וַיִּקְרָא֩ לְמֹשֶׁ֨ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֜ן), establishing a clear command structure: God → Moses/Aaron → People. The passage then prescribes precise hierarchical distinctions regarding who can participate in Passover (native-born Israelites, circumcised servants, but not uncircumcised foreigners or hired workers). Rules about inclusion, exclusion, and proper procedure are strictly delineated. The text concludes by emphasizing that the people 'did according to what the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron' (כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן), underscoring obedience to this hierarchical authority structure. Hierarchy is not discouraged but rather imposed and reinforced.
